thread:
maya: heads-up — noticed a burst of /v1/generate requests getting routed to cpu-small fallback around 02:48 UTC, several gold tenants hitting high p99
sam: any config or deploys at that time?
liam: no infra deploys, but runtime shows a spike in route.mismatch for /v1/generate
cb-bot: circuit-breaker: firing rwd-3b-quant pool us-east-1 at 2026-03-18T02:49:11Z, cb_rate=0.79
maya: quick check: are we matching on header `X-Tenant-Tier` or `x-tenant-tier`? gateway might be normalizing to lowercase which our matcher doesn't expect
jo: our route table has an explicit override for gold tenants mapping to lane premium and priority list [rwd-3b-quant, rwd-1.5b-int8], fallback cpu-small
liam: I pulled a sample: incoming header names are lowercased at nginx ingress, but our matcher was built assuming original case from client — mismatch causes default route path
anya: customer impact: 2% error increase and very high tail latency for a few sessions, billing unaffected but UX degraded
sam: immediate fixes we can do now:
- make matcher header lookup case-insensitive (config toggle)
- introduce a header-hint override (`x-override-lane`) we can set from control plane for affected tenants
- bump capacity on default lane temporarily
maya: let's avoid capacity bump if possible. Least blast radius is changing matcher to case-insensitive on canary
liam: I'll prepare a tiny patch: RouteMatcher.lookupHeader(key, caseSensitive=false)
jo: add logging to annotate each decision with `x-routing-decision` header so we can trace in APM
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by liam: gateway-route-matcher -> canary us-east-1 at 2026-03-18T02:55:00Z
sam: also add metric `route.header_case_mismatch{route="/v1/generate"}` so we can quantify how many requests were affected
maya: good, and set an alert threshold so we catch any regression
liam: canary logs show mismatch count dropped to near zero, cb-rate rwd-3b-quant -> 0.10 after 6 minutes
cb-bot: circuit-breaker: recovered rwd-3b-quant pool us-east-1 at 2026-03-18T03:01:21Z
anya: can we add a console UX item: in the request inspector show "effective route" and "matched headers" so support can quickly see why a request took a particular lane
jo: agreed. also document header normalization behaviour in routing docs and mark it in the console tooltip
sam: long-term we should formalize header precedence: host > path > headers, and normalize at ingress with deterministic semantics
liam: I'll add unit tests for header lookup cases (mixed case, multiple header occurrences, whitespace) and add an e2e that validates route override path
maya: for now I'll open an incident note and ping the affected customers with a short apology and explanation
anya: created PLAT-4837 (console-inspector) assigned to @jo
jo: adding docs PR referencing the new metric and the matcher toggle
maya: thanks. keeping thread open until 30m stable window passes
sam: one more thought — do we want a safety: if route rule references a header that never matched for N requests, emit a warning or highlight in console? Could help latent misconfigs
liam: yes, we can emit a config-lint warning at config load time if rules reference headers not present in sampled traffic
maya: nice. ok, closing loop after the postmortem write-up
deploy-bot: note: change rolled to prod at 2026-03-18T03:05:00Z
maya: prod metrics look healthy, will post the short postmortem to #incidents and close this thread :thumbsup:
